name: Router

hero.title: Every navigation runs your guards. The Back button too.
hero.lede: Nested routes, loaders that finish before the page renders, guards, middleware and leave blockers, and `await router.push()` tells you whether the navigation committed, was cancelled or was superseded. The same route table runs in the browser, on the server and in the experimental iOS and Android builds.

why.title: Routing with fewer ways to get it wrong.

items.title: The Back button runs the pipeline
items.text: Back and Forward go through blockers, middleware, guards and loaders like any `push()`. Sign out, press Back to a guarded page, and you land on `/login`. If a guard cancels, the URL and history position are restored.

items.title: Data before the page
items.text: Loaders run in parallel before the route commits and get an `AbortSignal` when a newer navigation supersedes them. `useLoaderData<LoaderData<typeof loader>>()` takes its type from the loader, so the two can't drift.

items.title: Navigation that reports back
items.text: `await router.push('/checkout')` resolves to `'committed'`, `'cancelled'` (a blocker, guard or middleware said no) or `'superseded'` (a newer navigation won). No guessing from the URL afterwards.

items.title: Accessible and smooth by default
items.text: The root `<RouterView>` announces each new page through a polite live region. Navigations run inside `document.startViewTransition()` where it exists, and skip the animation when the user asks for reduced motion.

difference.title: A signed-in area: the guard is a guard, not a loader.

before.label: React Router 8 (data mode)
before.caption: The auth check hides inside a loader that returns a redirect, so the settings route needs a loader just to guard it.

after.label: Pyreon
after.caption: Guards return `true`, `false` or a path. The loader types the component.

demo.title: Navigate a small app.
demo.text: Links, typed params, a loader and a guard. The settings page requires sign-in.
demo.spec: As in the reference (links, a typed param, a loader, a sign-in guard on Settings), plus two additions built on the real router: a status line that prints what each `router.push()` resolved to (`committed` or `cancelled`), and a Back button. Sign in, open Settings, sign out, press Back: the guard runs again and the view lands on Sign in.

limits.title: Guards aren't security
limits.text: A client-side guard only hides a page. Check access on the server too (with Zero, in route middleware or a `.server.ts` loader).

limits.title: Hash mode is the default
limits.text: Set `mode: 'history'` for clean URLs, and serve the app for every path.

limits.title: Loader params are strings
limits.text: A loader sees `params` as `Record<string, string>`. For params typed from the path, read them with `useRoute<'/user/:id'>()`, or let Zero's `typedRoutes` check every link.

limits.title: File-based routes come from Zero
limits.text: The router takes a route list. Zero builds that list from `src/routes` on the web; native apps declare it as an array.

comingFrom.title: Unsaved-changes protection
comingFrom.note: A Pyreon blocker is a predicate: return `true` to block. It may return a promise, so a custom dialog works too. It covers Back and Forward too, and is removed when the component unmounts.

comingFrom.title: Page number in the URL
comingFrom.note: Values arrive coerced to the declared type, and `setSearch` merges into the declared params (it replaces the history entry; query keys outside the schema are dropped). For richer rules, give the route a `validateSearch` function (or a Zod `.parse`) and read it with `useValidatedSearch()`.

recipes.title: A signed-in area that holds on Back
recipes.text: The guard reads a signal. Signed out, `/settings` redirects to `/login`, and pressing Back into it after signing out redirects again.
recipes.code:
import { signal } from '@pyreon/reactivity' import { createRouter } from '@pyreon/router' export const signedIn = signal(false) const Home = () =>

Home

const Login = () =>

Sign in

const Settings = () =>

Settings

export const router = createRouter({ mode: 'history', routes: [ { path: '/', component: Home }, { path: '/login', component: Login }, { path: '/settings', component: Settings, beforeEnter: () => signedIn() || '/login' }, ], }) await router.push('/settings') // 'committed', and you are on /login signedIn.set(true) await router.push('/settings') // 'committed', on /settings await router.push('/') signedIn.set(false) history.back() // the guard runs again: back on /login

recipes.title: Know when a navigation was refused
recipes.text: A blocker turns a push into `'cancelled'`, so a save-then-leave flow can tell the user instead of assuming it worked. Mount it only while there are unsaved edits: while a blocker is mounted, closing the tab asks first too.

recipes.title: One back stack per tab
recipes.text: A tab-bar app keeps a separate history per tab: switching tabs returns to where that tab was, and Back walks only the current tab's stack.
recipes.code:

Feed

const Search = () =>

Search

const Post = () =>

Post

export const router = createRouter({ mode: 'history', routes: [ { path: '/', component: Feed }, { path: '/post/:id', component: Post }, { path: '/search', component: Search }, { path: '/profile', component: Profile }, ], tabs: [ { name: 'home', root: '/' }, { name: 'search', root: '/search' }, { name: 'profile', root: '/profile' }, ], })

faq.a: Rarely as a bottleneck, which is the point: it stays out of the way at any route count. It is level with radix3, the fastest standalone matcher we measured, at 50 and 200 routes; Hono led at 10 routes, 1.91×, in the published run, measured before a harness fix that adds work to Hono's timed arm (PR #4142).

`ExtractParams<'/user/:id'>` is `{ id: string }`, and `useRoute<'/user/:id'>()().params.id` is typed. `createRouter<'home' | 'user'>` types named navigation, and Zero's `typedRoutes` makes a mistyped `<RouterLink to>` a compile error.

faq.q: Does it work with server rendering?
faq.a: Yes. Pass the request URL as `url`, and loaders run before the HTML is written; their data is serialised so hydration does not fetch again. Zero wires all of it, including server-only loaders in `.server.ts` files.

faq.q: Is it the same router on iOS and Android?
faq.a: The same API: `RouterProvider`, `RouterView`, `useNavigate`, `useParams`, `useLoaderData` and `beforeEnter`, lowered to SwiftUI's `NavigationStack` and to Compose on the experimental native targets. Inbound deep links route through it, cold and warm.

faq.q: Can I opt out of the announcements or transitions?
faq.a: `<RouterView announceRouteChanges={false} />` turns off the announcer, and `meta: { viewTransition: false }` skips the transition for one route.
